findings.description: The KMS key declares no `policy`, so AWS applies the default key policy that grants the account root principal `kms:*` on the key. Without an explicit least-privilege key policy, any principal that can obtain `kms:*` (or the relevant kms actions) through an IAM identity policy in the account inherits full administrative and cryptographic access to the key protecting the audit bucket data, with no resource-based constraint to restrict it.

`enable_key_rotation` is not set (defaults to false), so the customer-managed CMK used for the audit bucket is never automatically rotated. A long-lived key increases the volume of data encrypted under a single key material and extends the impact window if that material is ever compromised.
